newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-MAJOLI STRUGGLES ON THE GRASS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MAJOLI STRUGGLES ON THE GRASS.

text.p: French Open champion Iva Majoli struggled and stuttered through her first round match at Wimbledon on Monday and said the victory was almost as satisfying as winning the Paris Grand Slam title.

The 19-year-old Croatian, who has never got beyond the first round at Wimbledon, flung her arms in the air and whooped with joy after overcoming the horrors of grass and her 85th-ranked opponent Mariana Oliva Diaz of Argentina 2-6 6-0 6-3.
"Today when I won this match I was almost as happy as when I won the French," she said afterwards.
Majoli, conqueror of world number one Martina Hingis in Paris, looked like a tennis novice in the first set, hitting a host of errors and hanging back at the baseline.
Oliva Diaz's powerful forehand had the fourth seed scampering to retrieve shots as she tried to find her feet and judge the speed of the ball on the lush surface.
Two rain interruptions also disturbed Majoli's concentration and after she lost her serve for the second time she surrendered the set with a long forehand.
"I was very nervous today before the match, usually I am not so bad -- and she played really well," Majoli said.
But it was Oliva Diaz, 21, who then lost her nerve, relinquishing her tight control and handing easy winners to the Croatian.
Majoli's serve settled and she moved forward more, looking to hit early winners.
"I decided to go for it. I said to myself 'If you lose, better to lose in the right way than like a chicken,'" she said.
The two women traded service breaks in the final set until Majoli got the upper hand. She hit a punishing back hand return for match point and a stylish back hand pass down the line for victory.
"I started to move well and get more aggressive," she said. "I should do that more -- when I came in and attacked I won the point."
Majoli said she had had some words of advice about moving and keeping low to the ball from former Wimbledon champions Billie-Jean King and Martina Navratilova just before the match.
"It is my first victory here so I am really excited," she said, adding victory had given her renewed confidence.
"One match can change everything. My goal was to win the first round. If my game improves each match anything is possible on grass."
